requirement: Bulk import CSV/Excel with optional ID/source fields
evidence: Paste/CSV text imported through the real importer: 842 sites added from 988 lines. Only the URL column is read; no external ID or source field is kept (source_batch empty on all rows). Excel upload: NOT TESTED in the field test.

requirement: Incremental ingestion without re-importing
evidence: Second import of the same 60,000-URL list: 0 added, 60,000 duplicates, 19.9 s (extra_tests/t_import_60k.json). 19 of 23 duplicate-spelling rows were recognised.

requirement: Load URLs from existing DB / staging table
evidence: No database / staging-table loader exists (static check; the traceability matrix says 'not implemented').

requirement: Manual entry of one or more URLs
evidence: Pasted-text import works (importer function, 988 lines). The CLI has no import command. The web paste box was not exercised (UI is out of scope); the web upload endpoint was exercised with TestClient.

requirement: API submission single/bulk
evidence: No API submission (optional requirement). Only the HTML form posts to /import.

requirement: Normalize protocol, www, trailing slash; dedupe
evidence: http/https, www, case, trailing slash, path, query, default ports and spaces are normalised (19 of 23 duplicate rows MATCH). Missed: trailing-dot host (T0887), unicode vs punycode (T0898), scheme-relative '//host' (T0889), full-width characters (T0890). Ports and paths are always dropped.

requirement: Keep original URL exactly + source batch + source record ID
evidence: original_url is kept as received (stripped). source_batch is empty on 0 of 954 rows (the web layer never passes a batch); there is no source-record-ID column.

requirement: Domain extraction, invalid-URL handling, existing-record detection
evidence: Domain extraction, duplicate detection and invalid lists work. But one malformed line raised ValueError and lost the whole 988-row import (T0944), and 14 of 47 'must be invalid' inputs were not rejected cleanly at import (T0908, T0911, T0920, T0924, T0925, T0934, T0935, T0937, T0939, T0940, T0943, T0944, T0945, T0946).

requirement: Optional recrawl of processed sites
evidence: Manual re-crawl works (force / site ids; extra_tests/t_recrawl.json). No age-based or scheduled recrawl.

requirement: Reviewable batch import summary (added/duplicate/invalid)
evidence: Counts added/duplicate/invalid are returned and stored on the Job; the lists of duplicate/invalid rows are not stored. After the crash on T0944 no summary exists at all.

requirement: Ingest and queue 60,000+ without manual batching
evidence: The importer function ingested 60,000 URLs in 49.9 s with +13 MB memory. The web upload with default settings refuses a typical 60,000-line list (2.10 MB domain-only / 2.61 MB with paths against MAX_IMPORT_CHARS = 2,000,000; ~46,000-57,000 URLs fit).

requirement: Persistent job records, retry handling, failure reasons, progress
evidence: Job rows exist (kind, status, added/duplicates/invalid, note) and every failed site keeps a reason in crawl_error. No retry count, no per-site progress; the import job stays 'queued' forever.

requirement: Explicit lifecycle states, observable, recoverable
evidence: Kill -9 mid-run: 362 stuck 'crawling' rows reset by recover_abandoned, re-run crawled all 400, 0 rows lost (t_cancel_recover.json). But the states are only pending/crawling/crawled/empty/unreachable/blocked/robots_blocked/invalid/failed, and a cancel took 20.9 s to take effect.

requirement: Check format, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, redirect destination, TLS error, status, timeout
evidence: Format, DNS, HTTP status, timeout and TLS errors are detected (SSL rows: 17 of 17 judged rows MATCH as Unreachable). But a DNS failure is reported as 'invalid', not 'unreachable' (26 of 30 dead-domain rows), and the redirect destination and HTTP status are not stored.

requirement: Detect parked / for-sale domains
evidence: Parked / for-sale domains: 0 of 30 judged rows MATCH. All parked pages are stored as 'crawled' with junk text (e.g. T0637, T0644, T0647).

requirement: Detect under-construction / empty websites
evidence: Only text under 80 characters becomes 'empty'. Placeholder / default pages: 5 of 13 judged rows MATCH (nginx welcome page and 'Coming soon' stored as crawled: T0669, T0675, T0676). Thin / soft-404 pages: 2 of 12 MATCH.

requirement: Detect blocked / access-denied sites
evidence: Bot-challenge / access-denied sites: 24 of 24 judged rows MATCH (HTTP 401/403/429 -> 'blocked'; scenario challenge page T0816). Limit: detection is by status code; a 200-status challenge page was NOT TESTED.

requirement: Detect duplicate domain / canonical equivalent
evidence: Same-site spellings are merged (19 of 23). Not detected: canonical-tag or cross-domain redirect equivalence; trailing dot; punycode.

requirement: Status vocabulary (Pending..Requires Review)
evidence: Present: pending, crawled, failed, invalid, unreachable, blocked (+ crawling, empty, robots_blocked). Missing: Active, Redirected, Parked, Under Construction (empty is the nearest), Requires Review. 59 rows were judged MISMATCH only because the word cannot be expressed.

requirement: Crawl status usable in export (Completed/Partial/Failed/Blocked); partial keeps evidence
evidence: A partial crawl keeps its useful text and pages_crawled. There is no 'Partial' status and no pages-attempted count.

requirement: Crawl status separate from AI status
evidence: crawl_status and classification_status are separate columns, but a failed re-crawl keeps the old clean_text and hash while status says 'failed' (t_recrawl.json).

requirement: URL validation and safe-target checks before job created/queued
evidence: Literal private IPs and 'localhost' are refused at import. Names that resolve to loopback (lvh.me T0929, localtest.me) are accepted at import and refused at fetch. 127.1, 100.100.100.200, nas.lan, router.home.arpa are accepted at import.

requirement: Validate URL and every redirect target against SSRF
evidence: HTTP path: every hop checked (T0785 and T0791: redirect to 127.0.0.2 refused). Browser path: checks only the first URL; Chromium followed a JavaScript redirect to 127.0.0.2 and the internal page was stored (t_browser_ssrf.json). Guard also lets 100.64.0.0/10 (Alibaba metadata 100.100.100.200) through: 6 requests had to be stopped by the harness safety net.

requirement: Do not crawl whole sites
evidence: Crawled happy-path sites: pages p50 3, p95 8, max 8; 46 sites reached the 8-page cap.

requirement: Homepage always first
evidence: Homepage is always requested first (request logs for all 664 crawled sites).

requirement: Priority signals (About, Services, Products, Industries...)
evidence: The keyword lists match the requirement, but the substring skip-list runs first: 28 of 36 genuine business paths score 0 (t_score.json), e.g. /services/accounting, /products/compressors, /research.

requirement: Order of preference Home, About, Products, Services, Industries, Contact
evidence: Only three score tiers; inside a tier pages are ordered alphabetically by URL, not by the preferred order.

requirement: Discovery beyond URL patterns (titles, headings, nav, sitemap)
evidence: Discovery uses URL path and anchor text only. Gold-set recall of key pages is 33.5% (133/397); 120 gold pages were never requested because the ranking scored them 0, including non-English paths (16 of 17 tested) and '/who-we-serve' (T0850).

requirement: Do not spend budget on blog, tags, legal, careers, search, login, cart
evidence: Junk is skipped (blog, careers, privacy, login, cart all score 0) but so are many real business pages (see C03).

requirement: Configurable page budget 5-10; stop early when enough
evidence: Budget is 8 pages, editable only in config.py. Early stop at 12,000 characters: 194 of 530 crawled happy-path sites reached it; 89 gold pages were never requested because of the cap / early stop.

requirement: Sitemap-assisted discovery
evidence: Sitemap category: 20 of 20 rows MATCH. Robots Sitemap lines, indexes, .gz files and 50,000-URL / malformed / chain sitemaps were handled safely (T0846-T0850, endless chain T0986 passed). Only /sitemap.xml is tried when robots names none; found pages are ranked by path only (T0850 found /what-we-do but not /who-we-serve).

requirement: Prevent loops, duplicate fetches, unbounded discovery
evidence: 19 of 20 crawl-trap scenarios passed (all stayed within 10 pages and did not follow calendars, session IDs, facets, tag graphs). One failed: case/slash/index/utm duplicates were fetched more than once (T0984).

requirement: Canonical-URL handling
evidence: Canonical URLs are not used for dedupe or page choice (only written as a text line). T0984: /About, /about/, /ABOUT/ and /about/index.html fetched separately.

requirement: Async HTTP client first for every page
evidence: httpx async client first for every page; browser only after the HTTP result.

requirement: Handle redirects, codes, content types, timeouts, encodings
evidence: Redirects (limit 5: 7- and 9-hop chains fail, T0783, T0787), status codes, content types and timeouts handled. Encoding: Shift_JIS page with wrong header gave no text (T0871); a legitimate large page over 2 MB failed (T0868).

requirement: Extract text, metadata, headings, links, structured data
evidence: Title, meta description, headings, links and JSON-LD are read, but whole page bodies are deleted on 59 sites (see E02).

requirement: Content-quality check beyond HTTP 200
evidence: Quality = text length (80 chars) and script/shell words only. Soft-404, placeholder and thin pages mostly pass as 'crawled' (see B03).

requirement: Browser fallback only when needed
evidence: Browser is used only after HTTP (115 sites, 284 renders; 91 of 600 happy-path sites = 15%), never for every page. But it is ineffective: of 248 successful renders only 53 gave more extracted text, because the page is read right after DOMContentLoaded (4 of 7 testable sites give text after network idle).

requirement: Browser limits, skip heavy resources, same policies
evidence: Images/media/fonts blocked, 15 s timeout. A new Chromium is started for every render (284 launches, ~5 s each); ads / third-party scripts are not blocked; redirects and sub-resources inside the browser are not guard-checked (L-04).

requirement: Record HTTP vs browser per page; record browser failures
evidence: HTTP vs browser is recorded only as a 'Retrieved via' line inside clean_text. Browser failures (36 renders returned nothing) are not recorded anywhere.

requirement: Majority of active public sites crawlable without browser
evidence: Browser was needed on 91 of 600 happy-path rows (15%); 530 were crawled and the large majority of them by HTTP alone.

requirement: Limit response size, content types, decompression, redirects, browser resources
evidence: No cap on decompressed size: a 150 MB bomb cost +205 MB, a 600 MB bomb +941 MB, before the 2 MB check ran (t_bomb_*.json). No total-time cap: a slow-drip page held a worker 265 s (T0698); a 60 MB body was read for 27 s (T0843). Redirect depth (5) and content-type limits work.

requirement: Persist per site status/final URL/pages attempted & crawled; per page fields
evidence: Per site only status, error text, pages_crawled, last_crawled_at, content_hash are stored. Missing: final URL, HTTP status, pages attempted, and every per-page field (analysis.json database_fields).

requirement: Never pass raw HTML downstream
evidence: 0 of 664 stored texts contain raw HTML tags.

requirement: Retain title, meta, H1-H3, paragraphs/lists, names, CTAs, structured data
evidence: Headings, paragraphs, list items, title, meta description kept. h4-h6, tables, div text, buttons/CTAs dropped; and on 59 sites a class name on <body>/<html> made the crawler delete the whole page (11 of 14 sites tested in detail).

requirement: Remove CSS/JS, nav/footer, cookie banners, ads, legal, duplicates
evidence: Scripts, nav, footer, banners removed and repeated lines kept once. Over-removal is the problem: DROP_NAME_HINTS ('sidebar','cookie','modal','popup','newsletter') match substrings of <body>/<html> classes.

requirement: Structured data: JSON-LD, schema.org, OG, canonical; validated, source kept
evidence: JSON-LD organisation/product lines, Open Graph and canonical are appended as text; they cannot be told apart afterwards and are only JSON-parsed, not validated.

requirement: Boilerplate removal, nav/footer reduction, duplicate detection, hashing, quality checks
evidence: Exact repeated lines removed across pages; whole-profile SHA-256 stored. No near-duplicate detection; mirrored pages (T0985) still fetched up to the budget.

requirement: Reprocess only when content changed or explicit recrawl
evidence: The classification is kept when the new hash equals the old one (unit tests). The crawler still re-fetches every page first.

requirement: Store cleaned content separately from crawl metadata; optional raw with retention
evidence: clean_text sits in the same row as crawl metadata; no raw HTML store, no retention setting.

requirement: Output: cleaned, deduplicated per-page content with source URLs and extraction metadata
evidence: One consolidated profile with '=== PAGE: label | url' headers. No per-page records with extraction metadata.

requirement: Evidence-ready: source URL, timestamp, extraction method per fact
evidence: Source URL and retrieval method per page are in the text; the timestamp exists per site (last_crawled_at), not per page.

requirement: Record truncation (what was cut)
evidence: A '...[truncated]' marker was seen on 4 sites; what was cut is not recorded and the 12,000-character early stop is silent.

requirement: Sanitise extracted values; escape = + - @ for spreadsheets
evidence: Spreadsheet-formula escaping belongs to the export layer (Phase 3 scope, not run). The crawler stores values unmodified.

requirement: Capture contact/social signals and technology hints
evidence: No email / phone / social / technology capture (optional).

requirement: Respect robots.txt; documented robots policy
evidence: Disallow-all is respected (T0818 and real rows). robots.txt answering 5xx is treated as 'allow' (5 of 5 5xx rows crawled the homepage: T0822, T0833-T0836); no written robots policy; Crawl-delay: 10 ignored (T0820). Policy question for the project owner.

requirement: Descriptive User-Agent with real contact URL
evidence: A descriptive User-Agent is sent ('WebIntelligenceCrawler/1.0 (+internal research)') but with no real contact URL; a second bot name appears if a contact URL is configured. 11 of 21 'blocked' happy-path sites accept other User-Agents (design decision, see ISS-29).

requirement: Configurable per-domain rate and concurrency
evidence: Concurrency is configurable (CRAWL_CONCURRENCY), but a value in .env is ignored by the CLI (t_env_copy.json). Delay between pages is a constant (0.2 s): 562 of 673 multi-page sites had two requests less than 1 s apart.

requirement: Timeouts, exponential backoff, retry limits
evidence: Backoff is linear (1.5 s x attempt), one retry only; Retry-After is not read. Check 'honours Retry-After 5 s' failed on the 503 scenario (T0749). Exponential backoff requirement not met.

requirement: Slow/stop on repeated 429/403; record blocked; no bypass
evidence: No CAPTCHA / bot bypass is attempted (honest User-Agent). Later pages stop after 2 blocked responses. But 429/503 with Retry-After are retried within seconds (T0387: Retry-After 3600, next request after 0.05-1.6 s).

requirement: Track domain health
evidence: domain_stats is written (758 rows) but nothing in app/ ever reads it (static check).

requirement: Domain-level backoff/scheduling so one site never blocks the batch
evidence: A failing site never blocks the batch (semaphore + per-site catch-all), but there is no domain-level backoff memory or scheduler.

requirement: No unnecessary credentials/cookies/personal data stored
evidence: No cookies or credentials are written to the DB in the run (secret_stored = False), but original_url is stored as typed, so a URL with a password would be stored (static, importer.py). One shared in-memory cookie jar per run.

requirement: Failure reason + retry count per site; manual requeue; recrawl design
evidence: A failure reason is stored for every failed site; manual requeue works; there is no retry-count field.

requirement: Stable, reputable outbound networking
evidence: Environment property, not code. Test network: home connection in Lahore (recorded in environment.json).

requirement: Async queue-based processing; durable queue
evidence: Asynchronous, DB-claim based, restart-safe, but in-process asyncio with no durable queue. 1,000 sites in one call created 992 asyncio tasks at once (t_scale_local.json).

requirement: Bounded concurrency, backpressure, persistent scheduling, idempotent jobs, retry/recovery, progress
evidence: Bounded concurrency (semaphore), idempotent claim, recovery works. No back-pressure on task creation; progress is only a printed line.

requirement: Crawl workers independently scalable from AI workers
evidence: Crawler and AI have separate entry points, but independent scaling was not measured in Phase 1.

requirement: Metrics: success rate, latency, errors, throughput
evidence: app.report gives success rate and counts; no latency distribution or throughput. The harness measured them independently.

requirement: Structured logs, job tracking, error reporting; no silent swallow
evidence: Structured JSONL event log exists. Several failures are swallowed silently (browser errors return None, sitemap fetch errors ignored, robots errors fail open); a cancelled run leaves 'coroutine was never awaited'.

requirement: A failed website never interrupts the batch; actionable reason
evidence: 988 rows were judged without the crawl batch ever stopping and every failed site kept a reason. But one bad URL stopped the whole import (T0944).

requirement: Planning estimate only; no assumed worker count/runtime
evidence: The code never claims a 60,000-site runtime (report.py: production_ready False); this report quotes only measured values.

requirement: Benchmark on pilot before raising concurrency
evidence: README tells operators to start with ~100 sites; there is no crawl benchmark tool (benchmark.py times search/export only).

requirement: Full run with monitoring, retries and export checkpoints
evidence: Monitoring = log + report; backup, recover and cancel commands exist; no export checkpoints. The harness run resumed correctly from checkpoints.

requirement: PostgreSQL + migrations + schema/indexes; or justified SQLite
evidence: SQLite with ad-hoc ALTER TABLE column additions, no migration tool. README says a PostgreSQL move is possible but gives no justification against 60,000-site needs.

requirement: Crawl entities: websites, jobs, discovered pages, fetch attempts, content, pages, errors/retries
evidence: Tables: websites, jobs, domain_stats, evidence_records. No discovered-pages, page-fetch-attempts, per-page content or error/retry-history tables.

requirement: Timestamps, content hashes, processing metadata, Last Crawled At
evidence: last_crawled_at and content_hash exist per site; nothing per page.

requirement: Data for export columns (Record ID..Last Crawled At)
evidence: Present: original URL, normalized, crawl status, error, pages crawled, last crawled. Missing or empty: source/batch, final URL, HTTP status, pages attempted.

requirement: Data for Crawled Pages and Errors/Failed URLs sheets
evidence: No per-page rows and no error category / retry count / last-attempt fields to build the Crawled Pages and Errors sheets.

requirement: Representative pilot (countries, industries, tech, sizes); start ~100, then 500-1,000
evidence: Process item for the test itself: 988-row representative dataset, 100-row smoke subset first, then the full run.

requirement: Measure success, useful-content, discovery quality, fallback, latency, retries, resources, throughput
evidence: The crawler's own report measures success rate and browser-fallback sites only. This field test measured the rest (gold-set recall, fallback benefit, latency, retries, resources).

requirement: No production-ready / 60,000-in-X claims without benchmarks
evidence: The code makes no readiness claim; this report makes none beyond the measured runs.

requirement: Pilot validates discovery, blocking, extraction, runtime
evidence: Process item for the test itself.

requirement: Automated tests for the listed crawler areas
evidence: 154 tests pass offline, but crawler coverage is 91% (not 100%); browser.py 50%. Defects found by the field test sit in areas the tests do not exercise (browser SSRF, robots 5xx, DNS status).

requirement: Controlled fixtures (HTML, redirects, errors, empty, duplicates, sitemap, structured, JS)
evidence: Mock-transport fixtures exist for HTML, redirects, errors, sitemaps, structured data; JavaScript rendering is only mocked.

requirement: Tests do not crawl real sites
evidence: All 154 tests ran offline (Step 0).

requirement: Run tests after each phase; report actual results
evidence: README claims '108 passed / 100% coverage'; measured: 154 passed, crawler coverage 91%, whole app 88%.

requirement: Inspect before modifying; reuse working code
evidence: Coding rule for Phase 2 code. Baseline observations are scored under the matching functional requirements.

evidence: Coding rule for Phase 2 code. Baseline observations are scored under the matching functional requirements.

requirement: Config outside source code; no secrets committed
evidence: Coding rule for Phase 2 code. Baseline observations are scored under the matching functional requirements.

requirement: Migrations for schema changes; few dependencies; explain stack changes
evidence: Coding rule for Phase 2 code. Baseline observations are scored under the matching functional requirements.

requirement: Idempotent, recoverable jobs; meaningful logs
evidence: Coding rule for Phase 2 code. Baseline observations are scored under the matching functional requirements.

requirement: Do not invent results
evidence: Coding rule for Phase 2 code. Baseline observations are scored under the matching functional requirements.

evidence: Coding rule for Phase 2 code. Baseline observations are scored under the matching functional requirements.
